newsitem.title: USA: NASA moves up shuttle launch.
newsitem.headline: NASA moves up shuttle launch.

text.p: NASA managers moved up Tuesday's planned launch of the space shuttle Columbia in an attempt to dodge expected afternoon thunderstorms, U.S. space agency offcials said on Monday.
The shuttle's launch time on Tuesday would be moved 47 minutes earlier to 1:50 p.m. EDT (1750 GMT), shuttle programme manager Tommy Holloway said.
"We have the opportunity to launch a little earlier tomorrow to hopefully get out of town before the thunderstorms show up," he said.
U.S. Air Force meteorologists still offered a grim forecast for the shuttle's blastoff from Florida's Kennedy Space Centre, giving only a 10 percent chance of fair weather for the launch.
Thunderstorms and rain showers were expected to form along the east coast of Florida and there also was potential for severe weather which could damage an exposed shuttle on the launch pad.
"The bottom line is, the earlier we go in the day the better," launch weather officer Scott Jacobs told a news conference.
Engineers reported no technical problems with Columbia, the oldest of NASA's four space shuttles.
The winged spaceship is to make a second attempt at a 16-day research mission that was cut short in April after just five days because of a troublesome power generator.
